beats.beat: The company's product portfolio is divided into four categories: Functional Additives (FA), Chemically Modified Minerals (CMM), Soft Minerals (SM), and Hard Minerals (HM).
It does not have long-term agreements with customers or suppliers; sales are governed by individual purchase orders and raw materials are procured on a spot basis.
The top 10 customers accounted for approximately 59% of revenue from operations in each of fiscal 2015, 2016, and 2017.
Exports have been made to Nigeria, Saudi Arabia, and Sri Lanka, aggregating ₹1,068.18 lakh over the past five years.

Key competitive strengths include a diversified product portfolio and user base, import substitution opportunity, support from the holding company 20 Microns Ltd., product innovation through continuous R&D, and a strong management team.

beats.beat: Promoters are Mr. Chandresh S. Parikh, Mr. Atil C. Parikh, Mr. Rajesh C. Parikh, and 20 Microns Limited (the corporate promoter).
Promoters hold 89,48,270 equity shares, representing 99.76% of pre-issue paid-up equity. Promoter group (excluding promoters) holds 21,510 shares (0.24%).
Pre-issue paid-up capital is ₹897.00 lakh (89,70,000 shares of ₹10 each); authorised capital is ₹2,000 lakh.
The company has entered into related party transactions in the last five financial years and the six months ended September 30, 2017, as detailed on page 223 of the DRHP.

Governance flags from the DRHP: past instances of non-filing or delayed filing with the RoC; missing statutory licenses for the manufacturing facility at Plot 9-10, GIDC Waghodia; corporate logo not registered; and the company does not own premises for some of its facilities.

beats.beat: The specialty chemicals segment (excluding agrochemicals and dyestuff) was estimated at about ₹1,000 billion in fiscal 2017, growing at a 10–12% CAGR from fiscal 2014 to 2017.
CRISIL Research forecasts a 12–14% CAGR for the overall specialty chemicals industry going forward.

Within specialty chemicals, several segments are expected to grow at robust rates: polymer additives at 10% CAGR, construction and water chemicals at 15% CAGR, textiles and F&F at 12% CAGR, personal care at 15% CAGR, and surfactants at 13% CAGR.

Growth drivers include rising consumption, an expanding middle class (expected 148 million households by 2030), improved consumption standards, government initiatives (Draft National Chemical Policy, 100% FDI allowed, PCPIRs with proposed ₹9 trillion investments), and favourable global factors such as Chinese environmental regulations reducing output.
The industry is highly fragmented: SMEs account for 70–75% of market share, though a few large Indian players and global giants compete on innovation and scale.

Headwinds acknowledged in the filing: the chemicals sector has higher imports than exports, with import CAGR at 6.4% outpacing export CAGR of 6%; REACH regulations affect EU exports; GST came into effect from July 1, 2017, adding compliance requirements.

beats.beat: 20 Microns Nano Minerals Limited is a specialty chemicals company that processes and sells functional additives, chemically modified minerals, soft minerals, and hard minerals.
It has a long-term arrangement with its corporate promoter, 20 Microns Limited, to market and sell products through that network.
The company is raising capital through a fresh issue to fund a new manufacturing facility at Plot 336, GIDC Waghodia, Vadodara, Gujarat, and for general corporate purposes.
The equity shares are proposed to be listed on the SME platform of NSE (NSE EMERGE).

intro.purpose: Orient the reader: who the company is, what it does, what it is raising, and why it matters.

beats.beat: The issue is a fresh issue of equity shares; no offer for sale component is disclosed.

Net proceeds will be used primarily to fund capital expenditure for a new manufacturing facility at Plot 336, GIDC Waghodia, Vadodara, Gujarat, and for general corporate purposes. A secondary objective is to create a public market for the shares via listing on NSE EMERGE.
The book running lead manager is Vivro Financial Services Private Limited.
The registrar to the issue is Link Intime India Private Limited.
The exact issue size, price band, and number of shares are not stated in the DRHP excerpts provided.

beats.beat: Lack of long-term contracts: The company operates without long-term agreements with customers or raw material suppliers, relying on purchase orders. This exposes revenue and margins to spot pricing and demand volatility.

Negative operating cash flows: The company recorded negative net cash from operations in FY2017 (₹349.75 lakh outflow) and also in earlier years (FY2013, FY2014). Sustained negative cash flows could constrain growth and require additional financing.
Missing statutory licenses: The manufacturing facility at Plot 9-10, GIDC Waghodia, Vadodara, lacks required statutory licenses and approvals. The company may face penalties or disruptions.
Legal proceedings: The company, its promoters, group companies, and directors are parties to certain legal proceedings. Adverse outcomes could materially affect financial condition and operations.
Near-total promoter ownership: Promoters hold 99.76% of pre-issue equity, leaving minimal free float. This concentration could lead to governance risks and limited liquidity for public shareholders.
